questions.question: More than half of truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by:
questions.explanation: Rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors.
Does not help you drive more safely.
Can help you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous. Looking ahead helps you spot obstacles early so you can avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should brake:

options.text: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
As the vehicle is placed in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: If your trailer starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel left, then right.

questions.explanation: Release the brakes so your wheels can grip the road again. The trailer will then straighten out.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: You take a turn too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: You take a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too fast. Drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when towing trailers.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always completely raise landing gear before driving. If not fully raised, it can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These are difficult to operate and require caution.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle could move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will make it worse. Release the brakes instead to help your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal harder than normal.
Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
Press the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using ABS brakes, apply them the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause trailers to tip over. The last trailer is most likely to flip. Drivers should know how their vehicle moves and drive safely.

questions.question: Put the trailer air supply control in "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. After making sure the trailer moves freely, pull out the air supply control or put it in "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and check that the trailer does not move.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should:

options.text: Only be used for parking on a downhill slope.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure from the brakes, which will release the brakes holding the vehicle. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high:
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check the trailer height. If the trailer is too low, its nose can be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can make your trailer skid.

questions.question: Before a trip, how can you check that air flows to all trailers?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build, then send air to both brake lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air comes out, air is being supplied to the whole vehicle.

questions.question: Look into the back of the fifth wheel:

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When checking a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.explanation: Following the right steps to couple and uncouple trailers is important for safe driving. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services for help.
